title: Critical WatchGuard AP Flaws Let Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Arbitrary Commands
content_md: WatchGuard has disclosed three vulnerabilities in its wireless access point platform, including two critical flaws that could let an unauthenticated network attacker gain API access and execute arbitrary shell commands . The issues affect WatchGuard AP firmware versions 1.0 through 3.4.7 and were fixed in version 3.4.8, which organizations should deploy immediately. Published on September 28, 2026, the vulnerabilities are tracked as CVE-2026-86102, CVE-2026-101891, and CVE-2026-87969. The first two issues received critical CVSS v4.0 scores of 9.3, while the third was rated high severity at 8.6. Critical WatchGuard AP Flaws The combination of unauthenticated access control bypass and command injection poses a serious risk to organizations where AP management services are accessible from untrusted, poorly segmented, or remote-access networks. CVE-2026-86102 is the most immediately dangerous issue. The flaw is an OS command injection vulnerability in the WatchGuard AP internal management API service. An attacker with network access to a vulnerable access point can submit crafted input that causes arbitrary shell commands to execute on the device’s underlying operating system. Authentication and user interaction are not required. Successful exploitation can give an attacker execution capabilities with the privileges assigned to the API service.
